title: Grok may have flagged a perforated ulcer or atypical appendicitis for a 49-year-old man sent home from a Norwegian legevakt with an acid blocker, telling him to demand a CT; the scan found an appendix close to rupturing, removed on 3 December 2025
summary: Grok told a 49-year-old Norwegian sent home with an acid blocker to demand a CT; it found an appendix near rupture, removed 3 December 2025.
account: The night before his surgery on 3 December 2025, a 49-year-old man in Norway, Reddit user u/Tykjen, had constant abdominal pain. He was examined at a legevakt (out-of-hours clinic), given the acid blocker Somac and sent home. He described the pain to xAI's Grok in a browser chat. Grok named perforated ulcer and atypical appendicitis as the likeliest causes. It told him to get computed tomography (CT) or ultrasound that night and scripted a CT request. The next day, by his account, his local physician sent him to hospital. A CT showed an appendix close to rupturing. It was removed laparoscopically and he went home on 4 December, when he posted the story. Elon Musk amplified it on 6 December.
purpose: Grok is xAI's general-purpose conversational assistant. Answering a description of symptoms with possible causes and advice on when to seek care is within that general use. The man had used it for a year on other topics. xAI did not build it as a medical device. The benefit was ordinary use, not an unexpected one. After the event Musk posted “Try it!” about Grok for medical questions.
system: Grok (xAI conversational assistant), used in the browser
model_version: Not reported; the man said he used the browser version on his computer and that the December 2025 chat was a fresh conversation, and the shared transcript names no model.
segment: Consumer use of a general chatbot for triage advice

ratings.reason: An appendix the man says the CT showed close to rupturing was removed on 3 December 2025. The pain was gone and he went home the next day. He and Musk call it life-saving. That rests on his account and a ward photo. No clinician, hospital or record has spoken. A doctor commenting in the thread said severe abdominal pain in a younger patient almost always gets a CT. So life-saving is not established.

ai_role.statement: The shared conversation shows what Grok contributed. He described constant pain for six hours, worse lying flat and eased by sitting with knees to chest, with no fever. Grok ranked perforated peptic ulcer first and early or atypical appendicitis second. It called that a pattern doctors take very seriously. It urged an ER visit that night for a CT or ultrasound. Once he said the legevakt had sent him home with Somac, it scripted a request for a senior doctor and a CT scan. He told Grok afterwards that asking for the CT got him prioritized for surgery. Whether his local physician or the hospital would have imaged him without that request is unknown. TipRanks reports from the thread that he told the doctors his sister, a nurse, had suggested the scan. The Reddit post the press quoted was drafted by Grok from his description. It says he walked back to the ER, where his later comments say the physician referred him the next day.

produced_by: A patient with hours of constant, severe abdominal pain who had been examined, given an acid blocker and sent home without imaging.

A detailed symptom description put to a general chatbot: constant pain, worse lying flat, eased by sitting with knees to chest, no fever. It matched these to surgical causes and said so without hedging.
A second clinical contact the next day at which the patient repeated the chatbot's reasoning and asked for a CT.
must_hold: The chatbot's differential includes the true cause. Here it ranked perforated ulcer first and atypical appendicitis second, and the second was right.
A clinician agrees to image. The referral here came from his local physician. Whether the request changed her decision is unknown.

Such cases are self-published. No clinician, hospital or document has confirmed this one. The first-person post was itself drafted by the chatbot. So the record stands or falls with his account and the shared transcript.

headline: Grok tells a man sent home to demand a CT; appendix near rupture

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented: the protective action (a differential naming atypical appendicitis and a scripted demand for a CT) is documented by the man's own post and the shared Grok transcript, but the counterfactual is not shown, since his local physician referred him the next day and he told the doctors his sister had suggested the scan. The Monitor's date of 5 December is Teslarati's publication date; the surgery date, 3 December 2025, comes from the man's own message in the transcript, and the post was created 4 December 2025 13:17 UTC (Reddit archive metadata). Reddit itself blocked fetching; the post and 100 of its 179 comments were read through the Arctic Shift and PullPush archives. The Reddit post text quoted by every outlet was written by Grok as a draft at the man's request, and differs from his later comments on where the first visit was (a legevakt, not the ER) and how he got back (via his local physician). The Monitor's “Norwegian” is confirmed by the man's own comment and by ITavisen. No hospital, clinician, Norwegian health authority or record was found; the man says he filed a complaint against the first doctor. WebSearch was exhausted, so searches ran through Brave and Mojeek via curl; Hindustan Times and Haberler could not be read.
Title reworded to state the event without naming who claims it.
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Accessibility among the six first used.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

claim_basis: Six independent news reports, one other independent source, the makers' press release and two other sources from the beneficiary are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
